evidence.exact_quote: AfterTierEnd persists verification results, updates tier status in PRD/state, generates feedback for agent/user when verification fails, and handles failures as rework or complete-with-warnings according to policy.

items.impact: A crash between persistence, tier-status mutation, and feedback emission can leave contradictory durable and user-visible states, and the governing policy is not identified precisely enough to falsify an implementation.
items.statement: AfterTierEnd names all required effects and the broad rework/warning outcomes, but does not define their transactional order, idempotency, recovery after a partial write, or precedence when persistence and verification failures occur together.
items.title: AfterTierEnd effects lack atomicity and recovery semantics

evidence.exact_quote: The tier-end orchestrator example introduces tier_end verification integration, collecting artifacts and diff, calling verify_tier_end, mapping VerificationStatus to TierStatus, persisting results, updating tier status, and generating feedback when incomplete.

items.impact: Builders cannot tell which example steps are mandatory or how unmapped, timed-out, or failed verification results affect completion, producing incompatible orchestrator behavior.
items.statement: The integration sequence and status mapping are explicit, but the unit is framed as an example and does not specify whether ordering is normative, how unknown statuses map, or what happens when any collection, diff, verification, persistence, or feedback step fails.
items.title: Tier-end example does not close normative and failure behavior

evidence.exact_quote: EndVerificationResult preserves tier type, node id, status, wiring/acceptance/quality checks, findings, feedback, timestamp, and an algorithm that reruns wiring, acceptance criteria, and quality verification, maps critical/major findings to fail or warning, and generates verification feedback on failure.

items.impact: Without schema invariants and versioning, persisted results can disagree with findings, retries can overwrite evidence ambiguously, and consumers cannot safely migrate or audit records.
items.statement: The result fields and verification passes are enumerated, but the contract omits schema/version identity, uniqueness and retry identity, status-to-finding invariants, clock semantics, and behavior when an individual check errors rather than returns a finding.
items.title: EndVerificationResult lacks durable invariants and error-state semantics

evidence.exact_quote: run_quality_verification composes required reviewer subagent review and required quality gate criteria, accumulates findings from reviewer_result and quality_gate_result, and passes only when findings are empty.

items.impact: A required reviewer or gate that errors, times out, or returns no result could yield an empty finding set and therefore a false pass unless failure is converted to a finding by an explicit invariant.
items.statement: The pass oracle is mechanically clear for completed results, but the unit does not require successful completion of both required producers before evaluating findings.is_empty(), nor define deduplication or precedence between their findings.
items.title: Empty-findings pass oracle can fail open on producer failure

evidence.exact_quote: Reviewer subagent selection and invocation must resolve reviewer-capable entries through subagent registry using execution_unit_context and reviewer role metadata, use platform_specs functions and platform runner abstractions, avoid hardcoded code-reviewer or tier-only lookup, parse reviewer output as SubagentOutput, and preserve task_report feedback.

items.impact: Multiple eligible or maliciously registered reviewers can produce nondeterministic or unauthorized review execution without a deterministic ranking, trust policy, and no-eligible behavior.
items.statement: The DRY registry and platform abstraction boundary is explicit, but eligibility authority, deterministic tie-breaking, registry trust, capability verification, and the outcome when zero or multiple reviewer-capable entries match are undefined.
items.title: Reviewer registry selection lacks deterministic authority rules

evidence.exact_quote: Quality criteria are selected per tier type and run through quality check runners, preserving phase/task/subtask/iteration source tokens, document and design doc quality checks, linter and test coverage checks, no TODOs without tickets, and iteration quality checked at subtask level.

items.impact: Different runners or versions can apply different gates to the same tier, while unknown/custom tiers may silently receive no effective criteria.
items.statement: The criterion families and tier-era tokens are preserved, but the authoritative catalog representation, version binding, custom/unknown tier behavior, runner error semantics, and precise meaning of iteration checks at subtask level are not fixed.
items.title: Quality catalog is not versioned or total over tier types

evidence.exact_quote: End-tier verification error handling treats artifact collection failure as warning with Info finding, diff computation failure as logged warning and continue, reviewer subagent failure as fail with Critical finding because reviewer is required, and quality gate failure status according to severity.

items.impact: A Major quality-gate finding can be treated as a warning here while OSI-166 says Major blocks completion, so implementations can disagree on whether completion is legal.
items.statement: The error categories are usefully enumerated, but the preserved Major/Minor-to-warning mapping conflicts with the later Critical/Major blocking gate and no precedence rule reconciles warning status with completion blocking.
items.title: Quality-gate severity policy conflicts with remediation gate

evidence.exact_quote:
Start and end tier boundaries use the summary timing matrix to distinguish start-phase/task/subtask/iteration config-wiring
  and wiring/readiness checks from end-phase/task/subtask acceptance and quality verification.

items.impact: Iteration execution can display a start-verified state without a defined end verification, and the source itself preserves an unresolved GUI/backend readiness question that can mislead users.
items.statement: The matrix explicitly includes start-iteration but omits end-iteration, and the preserved readiness token asks whether readiness covers GUI, backend, steps, or gaps without resolving that scope.
items.title: Verification timing matrix leaves iteration end and readiness scope open

evidence.exact_quote:
Start/end verification gaps are closed by a canonical validation table maintained with orchestrator code; every row preserves
  config field, GUI control or UI source, backend consumer, applicable tier set, execution impact, and default or fallback
  behavior, and validate_config_wiring_for_tier uses that table as the source of truth.

items.impact: Duplicate, stale, or concurrently changed rows can validate the wrong GUI-to-backend wiring and present readiness that does not match the executed configuration.
items.statement: The required row dimensions and source-of-truth role are strong, but row identity, uniqueness, schema/versioning, consumer ownership, update synchronization, completeness oracle, and snapshot binding to a run are absent.
items.title: Canonical validation table lacks integrity and snapshot rules

evidence.exact_quote:
Start-of-phase, start-of-task, and start-of-subtask verification run config-wiring validation, readiness validation, operation-sequence
  validation, and known-gap detection before tier execution may start.

items.impact: Dependencies, configuration, or known gaps can change after validation but before execution, allowing a tier to start under conditions it never actually validated.
items.statement: The fail-closed start preconditions are explicit, but their ordering, shared snapshot, timeout/error treatment, freshness, invalidation, and atomic transition from verified to running are not defined.
items.title: Tier-start preconditions have a TOCTOU gap

evidence.exact_quote:
End-of-phase, end-of-task, and end-of-subtask verification run config-wiring re-checks, acceptance checks, quality review,
  and feedback emission for failed requirements, quality findings, or retry/remediation triggers.

items.impact: One failing or unavailable check can suppress later evidence or feedback, and consumers cannot infer whether a partially run sequence is complete.
items.statement: The required end checks and feedback targets are enumerated, but execution order, parallelism, timeout/cancellation behavior, whether all checks run after one fails, and the durable representation of partial completion are unspecified.
items.title: Tier-end verification has no partial-execution contract

evidence.exact_quote:
The canonical quality matrix maps tier types to required reviews for Phase, Task, Subtask, Iteration, and Interview phase,
  preserving artifact completeness, design correctness, code review, tests, lint/format, local retry acceptance, and downstream
  plan generation readiness criteria.

items.impact: The same tier can be judged under divergent matrices or subjective criteria, preventing reproducible certification and safe migration.
items.statement: The tier-to-review coverage is explicit, but the canonical artifact location, schema, version binding, owner, override policy, and machine-falsifiable pass oracle for each qualitative criterion are not supplied.
items.title: Quality matrix is named canonical without canonicalization mechanics

evidence.exact_quote:
The reviewer/quality path is mandatory at the end of every tier completion path, on retry paths after a failed tier is re-attempted,
  and when a quality gate failure feeds remediation back into the same tier.

items.impact: A missing, offline, rate-limited, or repeatedly failing reviewer can deadlock a tier or tempt an implementation to bypass a mandatory quality path.
items.statement: Mandatory reviewer participation closes an important bypass, but no terminal state, escalation, retry budget, or recovery contract exists for reviewer unavailability or repeated reviewer failure.
items.title: Mandatory reviewer path has no unavailability terminal state

evidence.exact_quote:
Verification failure policy requires execution-affecting mismatches and missing required upstream dependencies to fail,
  permits only non-execution-affecting display/observability/deferred mismatches to warn, and forbids performance concerns
  from weakening verification categories.

items.impact: A builder can label an execution-affecting mismatch as display-only or deferred, turning a required failure into a warning despite the invariant.
items.statement: The fail-versus-warn invariant is explicit and performance cannot waive categories, but the authority and deterministic oracle for classifying execution-affecting, display-only, observability-only, and deferred mismatches are not defined.
items.title: Failure-category invariant lacks a classification oracle

evidence.exact_quote:
Interview phases mirror the same lifecycle as other tiers: start uses wiring, readiness, and sequence checks; end uses wiring
  re-check, acceptance, and quality checks; interview-subagent-integration.md owns phase-specific quality criteria and UI/runtime
  consequences without inventing an alternate lifecycle.

items.impact: The interview owner can define UI/runtime consequences that accidentally alter lifecycle semantics, with no stated precedence or executable conformance test to catch drift.
items.statement: The lifecycle mirror and owner split are clear, but the allowed variation boundary, precedence on conflict, and oracle proving that phase-specific criteria do not invent an alternate lifecycle remain unspecified.
items.title: Interview lifecycle mirror lacks cross-document conformance rules

evidence.exact_quote:
When a tier fails because of issues outside its intended scope, the orchestrator retries once with the same config, then
  raises an Assistant chat CTA with review, skip, retry, and abort options; modal escalation is reserved for P0 risk such
  as possible data loss or workspace corruption, and unrelated failures must not be silently bypassed.

items.impact: An unauthorized or mistaken skip can bypass a failure despite the no-silent-bypass rule, while abort during possible corruption may leave unsafe partial state without rollback guidance.
items.statement: The retry count, CTA choices, and P0 modal threshold are explicit, but who may skip or abort, what each choice does to state and evidence, how the same-config retry avoids repeating side effects, and what recovery is required for data-loss risk are undefined.
items.title: Unrelated-failure CTA lacks authority and destructive-action contracts

evidence.exact_quote:
Verification failures produce structured feedback identifying the failing criterion, affected artifact or file when known,
  and expected next action, while rework loops reuse the existing incomplete-task/remediation flow rather than a separate
  ad hoc channel.

items.impact: Agent-supplied artifact paths or next actions can leak sensitive data, inject misleading instructions, overflow UI, or become inaccessible/unlocalizable without rendering and trust rules.
items.statement: The minimum feedback content and reuse of the remediation channel are clear, but schema/versioning, provenance, redaction, untrusted-content treatment, localization, accessibility, length limits, and behavior when the artifact is unknown are not defined.
items.title: Structured feedback lacks trust, privacy, and presentation constraints

evidence.exact_quote:
Puppet Master supports BeforeUnit and AfterUnit hooks that run automatically at Phase, Task, Subtask, and Iteration execution
  unit boundaries, separating lifecycle concerns such as tracking, state management, and validation from execution logic.

items.impact: Concurrent or nested unit execution can interleave stateful hooks, invoke them twice, or observe partial lifecycle state, defeating the promised separation from execution logic.
items.statement: The hook boundary and automatic participation are explicit, but ordering, exactly-once versus at-least-once delivery, nesting, reentrancy, cancellation, concurrency isolation, and recovery after hook/execution crashes are unspecified.
items.title: Lifecycle middleware lacks execution-order and concurrency semantics

evidence.exact_quote:
Platform hook registration uses orchestrator-level hooks as primary middleware while optionally integrating native platform
  hooks: Cursor hook files and events, Codex and Copilot CLI lifecycle outputs, Claude settings hooks with blocking/context
  behavior, and Gemini orchestrator-level Direct API hooks without native config files.

items.impact: User-level or repository hook files can inject untrusted behavior, and native plus orchestrator events can double-apply blocking, context, or state mutations.
items.statement: Provider coverage and orchestrator primacy are explicit, but trust precedence between repository and user hook files, signature/permission checks, event deduplication, timeout behavior, native-hook failure fallback, and version capability detection are absent.
items.title: Platform hook integration lacks trust and duplicate-event controls

evidence.exact_quote:
BeforeUnitContext carries execution identity, lane/worktree, role/account policy, tool use, tier type, platform/model, selected
  subagents, config snapshot, and known gaps into BeforeUnit hooks.

items.impact: Hooks may receive excessive account/config data, retain it beyond the run, or make decisions from mutable/oversized snapshots with unclear provenance.
items.statement: The context fields are comprehensive, but field types and optionality, snapshot immutability/version, redaction and least-privilege rules, hook access boundaries, size limits, serialization, and retention are unspecified.
items.title: BeforeUnitContext lacks privacy and snapshot integrity contracts

evidence.exact_quote:
AfterUnitContext carries execution identity, lane/worktree, role/account policy, tool use, tier type, platform, subagent
  output, completion status, and iteration count into AfterUnit hooks, with CompletionStatus variants for success, failure,
  and warning.

items.impact: Stale or mismatched output can be attached to a success/warning status, and concurrent attempts can update the wrong execution unit.
items.statement: The output and status variants are enumerated, but no invariant relates completion_status to subagent_output and findings, no attempt/iteration monotonicity is specified, and causality, timestamp, cancellation, and partial-output states are missing.
items.title: AfterUnitContext permits contradictory completion state

evidence.exact_quote:
BeforeUnitHook and AfterUnitHook traits are Send + Sync interfaces that execute against their respective context and expose
  a hook name.

items.impact: Hook implementations can block threads indefinitely, panic, ignore cancellation, or return errors inconsistently despite being shared across concurrent execution.
items.statement: Send + Sync and naming are explicit, but execute signatures, ownership/borrowing, sync versus async behavior, error type, timeout/cancellation, panic containment, and hook-name uniqueness are not fixed.
items.title: Hook traits omit execution and failure contracts

evidence.exact_quote:
BeforeUnitResult communicates active subagent selection, injected context, and block decisions, while AfterUnitResult communicates
  validation status, validation error, retry request, and retry reason.

items.impact: Results such as block=false with block_reason, validation_passed=true with validation_error, or request_retry=true without retry_reason can propagate contradictory control decisions.
items.statement: The result payload concepts are clear, but required/optional relationships, defaults, mutual exclusions, priority between block/selection/context and validation/retry fields, and validation oracles are absent.
items.title: Hook result contracts lack cross-field invariants

evidence.exact_quote:
HookRegistry stores before_unit_hooks and after_unit_hooks and exposes register_before_unit and register_after_unit registration
  methods.

items.impact: Duplicate registration, nondeterministic ordering, and mutation during execution can cause repeated or inconsistent lifecycle effects and unbounded hook accumulation.
items.statement: Storage and registration APIs are named, but hook identity, duplicate policy, ordering, removal/replacement, thread safety, snapshotting during execution, registry ownership, and lifecycle cleanup are not specified.
items.title: HookRegistry lacks ordering, identity, and mutation rules

evidence.exact_quote:
BeforeUnit hook execution runs each hook through safe_hook_main, short-circuits on block, preserves hook-provided active_subagent,
  accumulates injected contexts joined by blank lines, logs hook failures as warnings, and returns the combined BeforeUnitResult.

items.impact: Multiple hooks can select different subagents or inject conflicting/untrusted context, while a failed blocking hook is downgraded to a warning and execution may continue.
items.statement: Short-circuiting and context concatenation are explicit, but first/last-writer precedence for active_subagent, escaping and provenance for joined contexts, behavior of accumulated data on block, and fail-open treatment of hook errors are not reconciled.
items.title: BeforeUnit aggregation can fail open and merge conflicting authority

evidence.exact_quote:
AfterUnit hook execution runs each hook through safe_hook_main, short-circuits on validation failure, carries validation_error,
  request_retry, and retry_reason, logs hook failures as warnings, and returns the combined AfterUnitResult.

items.impact: An errored validation hook may be ignored, or an earlier retry request may be lost when a later validation failure short-circuits, allowing inconsistent completion and retry behavior.
items.statement: Validation short-circuiting is explicit, but the merge/precedence of multiple retry requests and reasons, preservation of earlier results, treatment of a hook execution error, and whether all validators must run are undefined.
items.title: AfterUnit aggregation lacks fail-closed retry and validation precedence

evidence.exact_quote:
safe_hook_main wraps hook execution, and built-in hooks ActiveSubagentTrackerHook, TierContextInjectorHook, StaleStatePrunerHook,
  and HandoffValidatorHook are always registered and integrated before and after subagent execution, updating ExecutionUnitContext.active_subagent
  even when platform-native hooks are also registered.

items.impact: A pruner, tracker, injector, validator, or native hook can race or overwrite active_subagent, and wrapper failures can leave the context partially mutated.
items.statement: Always-on built-ins close an optionality gap, but safe_hook_main containment guarantees, built-in ordering, duplicate-registration prevention, rollback of partial mutations, and precedence relative to native hooks are unspecified.
items.title: Built-in hook integration lacks ordering and mutation rollback

evidence.exact_quote:
Every subagent invocation must produce a structured handoff report with required fields; malformed output blocks completion
  and requests one retry, with a fail-safe path after retry.

items.impact: After the retry, builders can either block, warn, complete, or accept partial output under the undefined fail-safe, producing incompatible and potentially unsafe completion semantics.
items.statement: Required structured output and the one-retry rule are explicit, but the fail-safe path's state, minimum usable fields, authority, persistence, downstream visibility, and ability to complete are not defined here.
items.title: Structured handoff gate leaves post-retry fail-safe undefined

evidence.exact_quote:
BeforeHandoffValidation detects output format, loads the SubagentOutput schema, and prepares validation context; DuringHandoffValidation
  parses, validates required fields, types, and findings, extracts from text fallback, and requests one malformed-output retry;
  AfterHandoffValidation persists validation results, updates tier context, and handles post-retry failure as partial output
  with complete-with-warnings source disposition.

items.impact: A compatibility-only complete-with-warnings phrase can be implemented as a runtime completion state, contradicting retry/surface-error policy and permitting malformed output to advance.
items.statement: The three validation phases are well partitioned, but atomicity between persisted validation and tier-context update is absent, and the compatibility disposition is not translated into one authoritative runtime terminal state.
items.title: Handoff phase contract conflates source disposition and runtime state

evidence.exact_quote:
The SubagentOutput schema preserves task_report, optional downstream_context, findings, Finding fields, Severity values,
  and ValidationError variants for structured subagent handoff validation.

items.impact: Oversized, malicious, stale-version, or path-bearing output can exhaust resources, expose data, or be interpreted differently across providers and consumers.
items.statement: The core payload and error variants are enumerated, but schema versioning, unknown-field policy, maximum sizes/counts, encoding, path/line validation, provenance, redaction, and localization of human text are unspecified.
items.title: SubagentOutput schema lacks untrusted-input and evolution constraints

evidence.exact_quote:
src/platforms/output_parser.rs extends ParsedOutput with subagent_output and extends OutputParser with parse_subagent_output
  plus extract_subagent_output_from_text for platform-specific structured handoff parsing.

items.impact: Platform parsers can diverge on encoding, partial streams, error taxonomy, and resource consumption while still conforming nominally to the same trait.
items.statement: The extension points are explicit, but signatures, ownership, output/error distinction, streaming versus buffered behavior, stdout/stderr boundaries, maximum input, cancellation, and fallback invocation rules are not specified.
items.title: OutputParser extension lacks a common operational contract

evidence.exact_quote:
CursorOutputParser structured handoff parsing reads JSON output according to platform_specs, extracts task_report, downstream_context,
  and findings, and must not hardcode the output-format behavior.

items.impact: Valid JSON with the wrong envelope or duplicate/unknown fields can be accepted inconsistently, and platform-spec changes can silently alter interpretation.
items.statement: Platform-spec-driven format selection is a strong non-gap, but the expected JSON envelope, schema/version validation, duplicate-key policy, unknown fields, trailing output, maximum depth/size, and error-to-retry mapping are absent.
items.title: Cursor JSON parser lacks envelope and hostile-JSON rules

evidence.exact_quote:
Cursor text fallback extraction looks for Task Report and Findings markers, may use LLM extraction later, falls back to
  stdout as task_report, and records that findings cannot be reliably extracted from plain text.

items.impact: A malformed or adversarial response can force plain-text fallback, become a nonempty task_report with zero findings, and then satisfy the empty-findings pass oracle despite lost critical findings.
items.statement: The fallback honestly acknowledges unreliable findings extraction, but no fail-closed status, provenance flag, downstream restriction, or reviewer-visible warning prevents the synthesized empty findings vector from being treated as a valid pass.
items.title: Cursor text fallback creates a critical fail-open path

evidence.exact_quote:
HandoffValidator validates subagent output by using platform_specs-driven parser selection, trying structured parsing first,
  requesting retry for malformed output before max retries, and falling back to text extraction after retry exhaustion.

items.impact: Retry-exhausted text can bypass the structured schema and enter downstream state without a defined validity or completion restriction.
items.statement: Parser selection and retry ordering are explicit, but the unit does not say whether fallback output is revalidated against required fields, how retry exhaustion is represented, or whether partial/fallback output may satisfy completion and quality gates.
items.title: HandoffValidator does not define validity after text fallback

evidence.exact_quote:
Required-field validation rejects empty task_report and empty finding.description, and constrains finding severity to Critical,
  Major, Minor, or Info.

items.impact: Malformed categories, paths, line numbers, control characters, enormous strings, duplicate findings, or misleading whitespace can pass validation and poison persistence, UI, or completion logic.
items.statement: The two nonempty checks and severity enum are falsifiable, but the remaining Finding fields, Unicode/whitespace normalization, maximum sizes/counts, path confinement, line ranges, duplicates, and cross-field invariants are not validated.
items.title: Required-field validation is materially incomplete for untrusted findings

evidence.exact_quote:
The orchestrator subagent execution loop obtains the platform runner, executes the subagent, validates stdout/stderr through
  HandoffValidator, returns validated SubagentOutput on success, requests retry with SubagentOutput::example format instructions
  on malformed output, and after max retries warns and returns extracted partial output.

items.impact: Callers can treat retry-exhausted partial output as validated SubagentOutput and advance state or pass quality gates without any machine-enforced distinction.
items.statement: The loop and retry prompt are explicit, but return typing/provenance does not distinguish validated success from extracted partial output, and retry idempotency, runner side effects, cancellation, backoff, and caller obligations are absent.
items.title: Orchestrator loop erases validated-versus-partial provenance

evidence.exact_quote:
Handoff validation failure handling requests retry for JSON parse, missing field, and invalid severity failures, and after
  max retries proceeds with partial output while preserving complete-with-warnings source wording as a compatibility disposition.

items.impact: Implementations can interpret proceed-with-partial and complete-with-warnings as permission to complete, while the referenced stale retry/surface-error policy may require a surfaced failure.
items.statement: Retryable error classes are explicit and the warning phrase is labeled compatibility-only, but the authoritative post-retry runtime status, caller restrictions, downstream propagation, and recovery path are not stated in this unit.
items.title: Handoff failure policy preserves an unresolved terminal-state seam

evidence.exact_quote:
CodexOutputParser parses JSONL according to platform_specs, detects Turn/turn events and structured content, aggregates
  findings, and reports TextExtraction when no structured output is found.

items.impact: Malformed, duplicated, reordered, mixed-version, or huge event streams can produce lost or duplicated findings and ambiguous task reports.
items.statement: Platform-spec selection and no-output error behavior are explicit, but per-line parse failure policy, event ordering, duplicate/replayed Turn events, multiple structured outputs, aggregation precedence, stream limits, and unknown event versions are not defined.
items.title: Codex JSONL parser lacks stream integrity rules

evidence.exact_quote:
ClaudeOutputParser parses Claude structured output according to platform_specs, reads result.content or direct fields, attempts
  direct SubagentOutput parsing, and manually extracts task_report, downstream_context, and findings when needed.

items.impact: Conflicting result.content and direct fields can yield provider-version-dependent or attacker-controlled precedence, with manual extraction bypassing direct schema validation.
items.statement: The supported representations are named, but precedence on simultaneous or conflicting forms, array/multipart content handling, schema validation after manual extraction, unknown blocks, and resource limits are unspecified.
items.title: Claude parser does not resolve conflicting output representations

evidence.exact_quote:
GeminiOutputParser parses Gemini Direct API output according to platform_specs, extracts candidates[0].content.parts[0].text,
  tries to parse that text as SubagentOutput JSON, and reports TextExtraction when pattern extraction is required.

items.impact: Valid findings or task-report content in later parts/candidates can be silently ignored, while empty candidates, safety blocks, or non-text parts have no defined error behavior.
items.statement: The concrete extraction path is testable, but hard-selection of candidates[0].content.parts[0].text has no completeness proof, multi-part merge rule, finish/safety-state handling, bounds checks, or conflict policy.
items.title: Gemini parser can silently discard multi-part or alternate-candidate output

evidence.exact_quote:
CopilotOutputParser parses text according to platform_specs by combining stdout and stderr, extracting the Task Report section
  as required and Downstream Context as optional through regex section extraction.

items.impact: Diagnostics on stderr can forge headings, terminate sections, or contaminate the required task report; large or adversarial text can trigger expensive or ambiguous regex behavior.
items.statement: The required and optional sections are explicit, but concatenating stdout and stderr erases channel provenance, while duplicate headings, escaped headings, Markdown nesting, greedy matches, line endings, Unicode, and size/complexity limits are undefined.
items.title: Copilot section parser is vulnerable to channel and delimiter ambiguity

evidence.exact_quote:
Copilot findings parsing extracts Findings sections with severity, category, description, file, line, and suggestion fields,
  mapping Critical, Major, Minor, and Info strings to Severity values before returning SubagentOutput.

items.impact: Multiline or delimiter-bearing descriptions/suggestions can shift field boundaries, and hostile paths or line values can enter trusted downstream consumers.
items.statement: Finding fields and severity mapping are explicit, but section termination, field escaping, multiline values, unknown/localized severity, duplicate fields, path confinement, line validation, regex complexity, and parse-failure behavior are not defined.
items.title: Copilot findings regex lacks safe field grammar

evidence.exact_quote:
The hook-level validate_subagent_output function creates an output parser and delegates parse_subagent_output for output,
  stderr, and platform, while create_parser(platform) remains aligned with platform_specs-driven selection.

items.impact: An unsupported or stale platform identifier can select no parser or the wrong parser, and hook callers cannot reliably distinguish configuration failure from malformed output.
items.statement: Delegation and platform-spec alignment are explicit, but create_parser return/error behavior, unknown platform handling, spec-version binding, stdout/stderr ordering, and translation into hook validation/retry state are unspecified.
items.title: Hook validator lacks total parser-selection and error mapping

evidence.exact_quote:
AfterTier handoff validation logs platform, error type, and partial output snippet details, requests one retry with structured
  JSON output instruction, and after retry failure proceeds with partial output fail-safe while preserving complete-with-warnings
  source wording.

items.impact: Partial output logs can disclose secrets or personal data, and an unbounded or non-idempotent retry can repeat external effects before ambiguous partial output advances.
items.statement: The one-retry instruction and logged diagnostic fields are explicit, but snippet redaction/truncation/access/retention, retry identity and side-effect safety, offline/timeouts, and the fail-safe's authoritative runtime status are undefined.
items.title: AfterTier retry policy can leak output and repeat side effects

evidence.exact_quote:
Existing ParsedOutput integration populates output.subagent_output by attempting parse_subagent_output during platform output
  parsing, but the .ok() example must not silently drop parser failures contrary to structured handoff failure policy.

items.impact: The forbidden silent drop remains easy to implement because ParsedOutput has no specified field or result type carrying parse failure and provenance to callers.
items.statement: The negative constraint correctly rejects .ok() loss, but the replacement contract—error return versus explicit validation state, partial output representation, caller obligations, and compatibility migration—is not defined.
items.title: ParsedOutput forbids silent loss without defining error propagation

evidence.exact_quote:
Quality verification findings gate tier completion by severity: Critical and Major findings block completion and enter remediation,
  while Minor and Info findings are logged and proceed.

items.impact: The gate conflicts with OSI-127's Major-to-warning mapping, and untrusted parser output can understate severity to bypass remediation unless severity authority is validated independently.
items.statement: Critical/Major blocking and Minor/Info proceed behavior is clear, but precedence over OSI-127, handling of unknown or mixed severities, authority to assign severity, deduplication, severity changes on retry, and the exact remediation exit oracle are not defined.
items.title: Remediation severity gate conflicts and trusts parser-assigned severity

segments.summary: Reviewed persistence, tier-end integration, verification result schema, quality composition, reviewer selection, and tier quality catalog; found atomicity, fail-open, authority, and versioning gaps.

Reviewed end-error policy, timing and canonical matrices, and start/end verification; found a severity conflict, iteration asymmetry, table-integrity gaps, and missing snapshot and partial-run semantics.

Reviewed mandatory review, category invariants, interview mirroring, user escalation, feedback, and hook boundaries; found missing terminal, classification, authority, privacy, and concurrency contracts.

Reviewed platform registration and hook schemas/interfaces/results/registry; found native-hook trust risk, context privacy and causality gaps, and missing trait, result-invariant, and registry-order contracts.
Reviewed hook execution and integration plus structured handoff phases/schema; found fail-open hook aggregation, undefined fail-safe states, disposition/runtime conflict, and untrusted-schema limits.

Reviewed parser extension, Cursor formats, validator, required fields, and retry loop; found hostile-input gaps and multiple critical paths that erase validation provenance or convert missing findings into a pass.

Reviewed post-retry outcomes and Codex, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot parsers; found terminal-state ambiguity, stream and representation conflicts, candidate truncation, and channel/regex injection risk.

Reviewed Copilot findings, hook validation, AfterTier retry, ParsedOutput integration, and severity completion gate; found unsafe regex grammar, parser-selection holes, sensitive logging, lost-error shape, and a critical severity conflict.

cross_document_questions: Which runtime terminal state in Plans/Executor_Protocol.md governs retry-exhausted partial SubagentOutput, and does it forbid completion despite preserved complete-with-warnings source wording?
How does Plans/interview-subagent-integration.md prove its phase-specific UI/runtime consequences conform to the lifecycle mirror without changing start/end state transitions?
Which owner defines the durable schema, atomic write semantics, retention, and redaction for verification and handoff-validation state files?
